paper.title: School performance and retrospective voting: Evidence from local elections in Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability (p. 12): 'The authors do not have permission to share data.' The acknowledgements thank Susanne Jensen, Elena Mattana and Helena Skyt Nielsen 'for help with access to the Danish registry data'; …

registers.name_in_paper: Den Danske Valgdatabase (valgdatabase.dk), the official election statistics
registers.role: outcomes (vote share of the incumbent mayor's party at the polling station level) and controls (turnout, left support, share of valid votes)
linkage and treatment: identifies the school-age children living in each polling station area and the schools they attend, used to build pupil-weighted precinct GPA
controls: income, age, parental education and immigration status averaged over the parents of school children in each polling station district

registers.name_in_paper: GPAs in the school leaving exam published for each school by the Ministry for Education (Børne- og Undervisningsministeriet)
registers.role: treatment: school-level grade point averages in the 9th-grade leaving examination

linkages: Citizens are assigned to polling stations based on their residence, so school-age children living in a polling station area and the schools they attend are identified from the school register
Precinct-level GPA is a weighted average of the GPAs of the schools attended by the precinct's pupils, weighted by the number of those pupils
Sociodemographic characteristics are averaged over the parents of school children resident in the polling station district

sample.universe: Polling station districts (precincts) in Denmark's 98 municipalities at the municipal elections of 2009, 2013 and 2017
sample.unit_of_observation: precinct-election (polling station district by municipal election year)
selection_rules: Municipal elections of 2009, 2013 and 2017 are used; the 2013 and 2017 elections enter as first differences against 2009 and 2013
The 2005 election is not used because the 2007 structural reform (Strukturreformen) reduced the number of municipalities from 271 to 98
Register characteristics are observed for the population of all children in primary school and their parents between 2008 and 2019 (approx. 2.4 million individuals, ca. 40% of the whole population)
sample.n_observations: 2662 precinct-election observations (1982 with ΔGPA > 0 and 680 with ΔGPA < 0 in the Table 6 split)
sample.n_individuals: ca. 2.4 million individuals in the register population of primary-school children and their parents, 2008-2019

construction_notes: Precinct GPA is the pupil-weighted average of the 9th-grade leaving-exam GPA of the schools attended by children resident in the precinct (example given: 50% at a school with GPA 8.0 and 50% at a school with GPA 5.0 gives a precinct GPA of 6.5)

GPAPR: schools are ranked by GPA within each election year and assigned percentile ranks, aggregated to the precinct with pupil weights (example: 50% at a 90th-percentile school and 50% at a 50th-percentile school gives 0.7); ΔGPAPR = GPAPR_t − GPAPR_{t-4}
RRSP = GPA_t − (1/4)·Σ_{s=t-4}^{t-1} GPA_s (relative recent school performance)
Denmark uses a 7-point grading scale, with grade 12 corresponding to grade 'A' and grade −3 corresponding to grade 'F' on the ECTS scale

The income measure includes taxable and non-taxable salary after deductions for pension but before labor market contributions and special pension contributions, income from stock options, and possible illness and maternity pay (footnote 12)
LoC mayor = 1 if the mayor is from the Socialdemocrats or the Socialist People's Party, 0 if from Venstre or The Conservative People's Party
Left support = combined vote share for Socialdemocrats, Socialistisk Folkeparti, Enhedslisten and Alternativet in the previous election
Mayor-from-largest = 1 if the incumbent mayor's party won the most votes in the previous election; Congruence = 1 if the incumbent mayor's party is also in office at the national level
Heterogeneity indicators are built by classifying precincts as above or below the median precinct on the characteristic in question and interacting the indicator with ΔGPA

claims.statement: In pooled cross-sectional OLS with municipality and election-year fixed effects and no further controls, a one-point increase in the precinct's pupil-weighted school GPA since the previous election is associated with a higher change in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party.

treatment.label: ΔGPA — change in the precinct-weighted grade point average of the schools attended by pupils living in the polling station district

register_source.value: School register (identifies the school-age children resident in each polling station district and the schools they attend) linked to GPAs published by the Ministry of Children and Education; the paper names no Statistics Denmark variable code

definition.value: ΔGPA_t = GPA_t − GPA_{t-4}, where precinct-level GPA is the average of the school-leaving (9th grade) grade point averages of the schools attended by the precinct's pupils, weighted by the number of the precinct's pupils at each school. GPA is on the Danish 7-point scale; sample mean of ΔGPA 0.310, SD 0.580 (Table 1).

timing.value: Four-year difference between the GPA published in the election year (published June to early August, before the November election) and the GPA at the previous municipal election

outcome.label: ΔSMP — change in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party in the polling station district

register_source.value: Den Danske Valgdatabase (valgdatabase.dk); official municipal election statistics — not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: The difference in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party in polling station i between the current municipal election year t and the municipal election four years before (2013 vs 2009, 2017 vs 2013). Mean 0.001, SD 0.084 (Table 1).

timing.value: Measured at the November municipal elections of 2013 and 2017, each differenced against the preceding election (2009, 2013).

units.value: share of the vote (0–1 scale) per one-point increase in precinct GPA (Danish 7-point scale)

estimand.target_population: Polling station districts in Danish municipalities at the 2013 and 2017 municipal elections
estimand.time_horizon: Both variables are four-year first differences between consecutive municipal elections; the vote-share change is measured at the election, the school performance change over the preceding electoral period

population.description: Danish polling station districts (precincts) at the 2013 and 2017 municipal elections, each differenced against the preceding election (2009 and 2013)
population.period: Municipal elections of 2009, 2013 and 2017 (differences for 2013 and 2017); register variables observed for all children in primary school and their parents between 2008 and 2019
subgroups_defined: above- vs below-median share with a university degree
above- vs below-median share of native Danes
precincts with improving vs worsening GPA
population.selection: The 2005 election is excluded because the 2007 structural reform (Strukturreformen) cut the number of municipalities from 271 to 98; the analysis sample is the 2662 precinct-election observations with the required election and school data

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-precinct variation in the four-year change in pupil-weighted school performance within municipality-election cells; no exogenous shock or reform is used for identification.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on municipality and election-year fixed effects and the included precinct- and municipality-level controls, the change in a precinct's school performance is unrelated to other determinants of the change in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper reports the coefficient under successive control sets (no controls, demographic controls, demographic plus political controls) across the columns of its tables and notes that the result holds when demographic and political factors are controlled for.

key_assumptions.assumption: Voters can observe school performance before voting: school grades are published between June and early August, so the election-year results are available before the November municipal elections.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Institutional description of the publication schedule and of the Ministry's web tool and media coverage (Section 2.2).

key_assumptions.assumption: Voters attribute school performance to the municipal council and the incumbent mayor's party, i.e. responsibility for the folkeskole is correctly assigned to the municipal level.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Survey evidence on the electoral salience of the folkeskole and on voters' ability to identify the mayoral party; folkeskole is the largest municipal spending item (16% of the budget).

key_assumptions.assumption: Polling station districts approximate school catchment areas, so the pupil-weighted school GPA measures the school performance experienced by the voters of that precinct.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued in Section 3.1; precinct-level GPA is constructed as a pupil-weighted average over the schools actually attended by children resident in the precinct.

key_assumptions.assumption: The grading scale is comparable over time: exams are nationally standardised and graded by appointed censors, and the authors see no trend such as grade inflation over the study period.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Section 2.2; the authors state they see no signs of a trend over the period of the study.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference across polling station districts: the school performance change of one precinct does not affect the vote-share change of another precinct.

threats_discussed: Voters' perception of school performance differs from the actual measured outcome and is moderated by the media
Pupil-level factors such as socio-economic status explain a large share of differences in academic performance, so GPA is only partly under municipal control
Mayors and councils are responsible for many other outcomes (crime, elderly care, roads) that are not observed
Mayoral posts are allocated by coalition negotiation rather than directly by the vote, and coalition vote shares are not analysed
robustness_checks: Adding demographic and then political controls (columns of Tables 2 and 3)
Alternative school performance measure: change in the precinct-weighted percentile rank (ΔGPAPR)
Alternative measure: relative recent school performance RRSP (Table A.3)
Precinct fixed effects (Tables 3, A.2, A.3, A.4) alongside pooled cross-sectional OLS
Allowing the slope to differ by election year, with Wald tests (Tables A.1, A.2, A.3, 6)
Splitting the sample by the sign of the GPA change (Table 6)
unresolved_confounders: Voters' perception of outcomes, which usually differs from actual outcomes and is moderated by the media (stated in the conclusion as difficult to control for)
Changes in other municipal outcomes (crime rates, services for the elderly, condition of the roads) that are not observed

register_source.value: School register (identifies the school-age children resident in each polling station district and the schools they attend) linked to GPAs published by the Ministry of Children and Education; the paper names no Statistics Denmark variable code

definition.value: ΔGPA_t = GPA_t − GPA_{t-4}, where precinct-level GPA is the average of the school-leaving (9th grade) grade point averages of the schools attended by the precinct's pupils, weighted by the number of the precinct's pupils at each school. GPA is on the Danish 7-point scale; sample mean of ΔGPA 0.310, SD 0.580 (Table 1).

timing.value: Four-year difference between the GPA published in the election year (published June to early August, before the November election) and the GPA at the previous municipal election

outcome.label: ΔSMP — change in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party in the polling station district

register_source.value: Den Danske Valgdatabase (valgdatabase.dk); official municipal election statistics — not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: The difference in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party in polling station i between the current municipal election year t and the municipal election four years before (2013 vs 2009, 2017 vs 2013). Mean 0.001, SD 0.084 (Table 1).

timing.value: Measured at the November municipal elections of 2013 and 2017, each differenced against the preceding election (2009, 2013).

units.value: share of the vote (0–1 scale) per one-point increase in precinct GPA (Danish 7-point scale)

estimand.target_population: Polling station districts in Danish municipalities at the 2013 and 2017 municipal elections
estimand.time_horizon: Both variables are four-year first differences between consecutive municipal elections; the vote-share change is measured at the election, the school performance change over the preceding electoral period

population.description: Danish polling station districts (precincts) at the 2013 and 2017 municipal elections, each differenced against the preceding election (2009 and 2013)
population.period: Municipal elections of 2009, 2013 and 2017 (differences for 2013 and 2017); register variables observed for all children in primary school and their parents between 2008 and 2019
subgroups_defined: above- vs below-median share with a university degree
above- vs below-median share of native Danes
precincts with improving vs worsening GPA
population.selection: The 2005 election is excluded because the 2007 structural reform (Strukturreformen) cut the number of municipalities from 271 to 98; the analysis sample is the 2662 precinct-election observations with the required election and school data

identification.source_of_variation: Within-precinct variation over the two election periods in the four-year change in pupil-weighted school performance, net of precinct and election-year fixed effects.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on precinct and election-year fixed effects and the included controls, within-precinct variation in the change in school performance is unrelated to other within-precinct determinants of the change in the vote share of the incumbent mayor's party.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper argues that precinct fixed effects eliminate between-precinct differences stemming from underlying precinct-specific particularities, and reports the coefficient under successive control sets.

key_assumptions.assumption: Voters can observe school performance before voting: school grades are published between June and early August, so the election-year results are available before the November municipal elections.
